answer: A mesh of weather stations stays honest when every new identity must keep a distinct physical sensor alive at a different vertex of the network, streaming live readings only a real device at a real place can produce. The first fake costs one sensor, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 sensors. Bulk farming fails because each sensor needs its own rooftop and its own sable housing, and one operator cannot install twenty devices at once, like a mirror that reflects only the face standing before it. Readings are cross-checked against neighbours.
